name: The Walkthrough Points At Cells Whose Answer It Knows
note: KP-18 (2026-11-06). The finders check every answer against the solution before returning it, so a wrong deduction usually turns into no target rather than a wrong one — which is why several of these fail on how often a target is found, not on a wrong answer.

mutations.name: a wrong entry counts as a fact
mutations.why: A player's wrong digit left on the board would rule digits out of other cells; the walkthrough could then call a cell a single when it is not.
mutations.expectFailure: a wrong entry was taken as a fact

mutations.name: the cage's last cell is given the whole sum
mutations.why: The step's whole lesson is the sum minus the cells already there.
mutations.expectFailure: a last cell of a cage on every killer Lv.1 board

mutations.name: the rule of 45 forgets the filled cells outside the cages
mutations.why: 45 minus the cages inside is the sum of everything else, not of the one open cell.
mutations.expectFailure: a rule-of-45 cell on at least 80%

mutations.name: the rule of 45 points at a cage's last open cell
mutations.why: That cell is the step before (cage sum minus the rest); shown again as the rule of 45 it teaches nothing new.
mutations.expectFailure: is not just the last open cell of its own cage

mutations.name: a note cell may have one candidate
mutations.why: A cell with one candidate is the single, not a cell to think over with notes.
mutations.find: if (cands.length >= 2 && cands.length <= 4) return { r, c, cands };
mutations.expectFailure: a note cell has 2 to 4 candidates

mutations.name: a new step sees the last step's cell
mutations.why: For one render after a step ends the next one still had the last cell, already filled, and moved on at once: the killer walkthrough skipped the rule of 45.
mutations.find: const target = picked.id === id ? picked.target : null;
mutations.expectFailure: the target belongs to the step that picked it
